entity: ProvStore (openprovenance.org), the public repository for W3C PROV provenance documents, storing, browsing and managing them via a Web interface or a REST API; built and led by Trung Dong Huynh (paper 'ProvStore: A Public Provenance Repository', IPAW 2014, LNCS, doi:10.1007/978-3-319-16462-5_32), run at the University of Southampton from 2013 and at King's College London from 2018, retired in December 2024 (the maintainer's page, updated 12 September 2026), while the OpenProvenance landing page says 'ProvStore is coming back soon'; formalized in the provenance meta-aggregator census record of 2026-10-29 (provenanceerasure.org/aggregators/provstore/)
row_type: C (a public entity on which the archive bears: a provenance repository, retired; an entity of the provenance meta-aggregator)

classes_note: Two classes, sourced from the field by locus and matching the census's own kind and lineage for the entity (kind 'repository (retired)'; lineage 'computational lineage'; provenance_object 'a W3C PROV document'): the W3C PROV standards and the infrastructure that stores and processes PROV documents (B1, B3, B4, B9), and provenance repositories as such (B1, B3, B4, B7). The aliases are the entity's name (with and without the space), its host and operator name OpenProvenance (which also names the community model OPM's site; a candidate on 'Open Provenance Model' is the predecessor model, read and not admitted as the entity), the maintainer (Trung Dong Huynh, 'trungdong' his handle and GitHub pages host) and the paper's DOI suffix. The four letters 'PROV' alone are not an alias: they are also the homonyms of T (PROV Tokyo, PROV Exam) and the W3C standard's name, which is a class here. Admission by reading (§3.4): D where the archive names ProvStore, OpenProvenance or its maintainer and says something of it; O-class where an archive sentence applies an archive category (semantic provenance, provenance erasure, the dimensions of provenance, the Provenance Erasure Rate, the archive's provenance infrastructure) to W3C PROV or to provenance repositories as a class; a bare listing of 'W3C PROV' among anchors or keywords, a reference line or a citation-list entry is not a claim.
